# LRN International GCSE Hospitality (7146)
## Examiner and Moderator Marking Guide

This guide applies to all live series. It is written to be used alongside the question-paper-specific mark schemes, which supply **indicative content only** ("Suggested response"). Where the published mark schemes do not carry formal level descriptors, the standardised bands in Section 3 below are the awarding house standard and must be applied consistently.

---

## 1. Assessment Objectives

| AO | What it rewards |
|---|---|
| **AO1** | Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of food, cooking and nutrition — and, by extension across the subject content, of the industry, its business structures, customer service and team working. Recall of facts, terminology, temperatures, categories, named bodies. |
| **AO2** | Apply knowledge and understanding. Transfer of recalled content into the given situation — the hotel, restaurant, customer type or team problem set out in the stem. |
| **AO3** | Plan, prepare, cook and present dishes combining appropriate techniques. Assessed **only** through Paper 2-B (portfolio/practical). |
| **AO4** | Analyse and evaluate different aspects of food, cooking and nutrition, including food made by themselves and others — including reasoned judgement on consequences, benefits, limitations and impact. |

**Weightings by paper:**

| AO | Paper 1 | Paper 2-A | Paper 2-B |
|---|---|---|---|
| AO1 | 50% | 50% | 0% |
| AO2 | 30% | 30% | 0% |
| AO3 | 0% | 0% | 75% |
| AO4 | 20% | 20% | 25% |

**Marker implication:** roughly half of every written paper is recall-driven and must be marked point-by-point without requiring development. The AO4 share (20% of each written paper) sits almost entirely in the extended/scenario responses — a candidate who only recalls, and never draws out consequence or benefit, cannot reach the top band on those items.

Note that although the AO statements are phrased around "food, cooking and nutrition," they are applied across the whole subject content (Units 1–5). Read AO1 as "knowledge and understanding of the taught content," AO4 as "analysis and evaluation of the taught content."

---

## 2. Paper Structure

### Paper 1 — 1 hour, 50 marks
- **Section A (Objective), 25 marks.** 25 multiple-choice items, five options each (A–E), **1 mark each**. All must be attempted. Answered on a machine-readable sheet in soft pencil.
- **Section B (Subjective), 25 marks.** Short-answer and tabular questions, typically **2–5 marks** each. Tariffs are printed in square brackets. Question types seen: two-cell and five-row completion tables, "state two…", "describe two…", "list three…", single-fact temperature statements.
- Predominantly AO1 with AO2 in the applied short answers; AO4 credit sits in the "describe/explain" items where a reason or consequence is required.

### Paper 2-A — 1 hour, 50 marks
- **Scenario-based responses only.** Extended written questions built on a workplace vignette, each carrying **10 marks** and each opening with "Scenario:" followed by "Required:".
- Each scenario names an output form — a description, a summary statement, content for a maximum of two PowerPoint slides, a guidance document extract. The required form is part of the task.
- Scenarios are routinely **two-part** ("(i) … and (ii) …"). Both parts carry roughly equal weight.

### Paper 2-B — Portfolio Assessment (including Practical Assessment Task)
Centre-delivered, externally moderated. The portfolio **must** contain all three mandatory elements:
1. Investigation of a current food-related issue affecting the hospitality industry, with documented conclusions and a presentation to a group/mentor (Unit 1, LO4).
2. Review of customer service needs and expectations within a sector of the industry, with documented conclusions and presentation (Unit 2, LO3).
3. Plan, cost, cook, finish and serve a **3-course meal** — starter, main, dessert (Unit 4, LO4).

A portfolio missing any one of the three elements is incomplete and cannot be awarded a mark reflecting full coverage; moderators must report this rather than compensate. AO3 (75%) is evidenced by the practical execution — technique, safe and hygienic working, finish and service. AO4 (25%) is evidenced by the costing rationale, conclusions drawn, and evaluation of the candidate's own and others' work.

---

## 3. Band Descriptors — Extended and Scenario Responses

The published mark schemes give a "Suggested response" rather than banded wording. Apply the following standardised bands to every 10-mark Paper 2-A item, and the reduced version below to Section B items of 3 marks and above. Award the band **best fitting** the answer as a whole; do not require every bullet.

### 10-mark scenario items

**Band 4 — 9–10 marks**
Both required parts (i) and (ii) are addressed and are **balanced**. Content is accurate, technical and **specifically exemplified** — named professional bodies, named regulatory sources or lists, named ingredient/allergen categories, named assistive provisions, named team-development mechanisms. The response is **applied to the scenario** given (the restaurant, the team, the job role), not delivered as generic theory. There is clear analysis or evaluation: benefits, consequences or impact on the business, staff and customers are drawn out. The response is presented in the **form required** (summary statement, slide content, description). Range is evident — the candidate offers a spread of distinct points rather than one point restated.

**Band 3 — 7–8 marks**
Both parts addressed but one is thinner than the other, or coverage is sound but exemplification is partly generic. Content accurate. Some application to the scenario. Some evaluative comment present, but it is asserted rather than developed. Required form largely observed.

**Band 2 — 5–6 marks**
Both parts attempted but at least one is superficial, **or** only one part is answered well and the other is absent. Points are largely correct but presented as a list with limited development. Little or no application to the specific scenario — the answer would read the same for any employer. Evaluation minimal.

**Band 1 — 3–4 marks**
Fragmentary. A small number of relevant points, undeveloped, with errors or confusions present. Only one required part addressed. No evaluation. Form of response ignored.

**0–2 marks**
Isolated relevant words or a single valid point; or the response is largely irrelevant to the task set. Award 0 for a blank response or one containing nothing creditable.

### 3–5 mark structured items (Paper 1 Section B)
- **Full marks:** the exact number of discrete, correct, non-overlapping responses requested, each meeting the demand of the command word (a "describe" answer must carry a qualifying detail; a "list" answer need not).
- **Partial marks:** award one mark for each valid discrete response up to the tariff. Where a table has five rows for five marks, mark **row by row**; a wrong or blank row loses only that mark.
- Where a question asks for *two* points and the candidate gives four, mark the **first two** unless the paper-specific mark scheme directs otherwise, and do not penalise the extra material unless it contradicts the creditable points.

---

## 4. Command Words

| Command | Requirement for credit |
|---|---|
| **State / List / Identify** | A correct term, figure or example. No supporting detail needed. One mark per item to the tariff. Bullet points fully acceptable. |
| **Define** | The term or process plus what it *means* or *involves*. Naming a cooking method alone does not satisfy "define one way in which food can be cooked" — the answer must say what the method entails (medium, vessel, temperature or mechanism). |
| **Describe** | The point plus a qualifying detail that shows what it looks like in practice. "Improves skills" is a bald point; "improves customer-service skills through daily contact with guests" is a description. |
| **Explain** | The point plus *why* or *how* — a causal link. An "explain" answer with no reasoning connective (because, so that, which means, leading to) rarely reaches the mark. |
| **Outline** | The main features in brief; less depth than "explain," more than "state." |
| **Investigate / Review / Draw conclusions / Present findings** (portfolio and scenario) | Evidence of enquiry (sources, data, observation), a synthesised judgement, and communication of it to an audience. Findings without conclusions cap the mark. |
| **Analyse / Evaluate** (AO4) | Break the issue into its components and weigh them; state impact or consequence for the business, customer or employee. Judgement must be supported, not asserted. |
| **Plan / Prepare / Cook / Finish and serve** (AO3) | Assessed on execution and outcome, not on written description of intent. |

Where a scenario says "Produce a summary of…" or "a maximum of two slides," the instruction is part of the demand. Excessive length beyond a stated limit is not itself penalised in marks, but content must be selected and prioritised, which the top band requires.

---

## 5. Marking Conventions

**Section A (MCQ).** One mark per correct letter. No mark where two or more options are indicated, where the response is erased ambiguously, or where the answer is written outside the response grid. There is no penalty for a wrong answer; no negative marking. Do not mark answers written on the question paper.

**Point-based credit.** One mark per creditable point unless the paper-specific scheme states otherwise. No half marks. Marks are awarded, never deducted for surrounding error, **except** where an error negates the creditable point or introduces an unsafe practice (see below).

**Alternatives to the model answer.** The "Suggested response" is illustrative and **not exhaustive**. Credit any answer that is technically correct, relevant to the demand, and consistent with recognised hospitality practice — including practice from the candidate's own country. Candidates are international; accept non-UK equivalents for professional/regulatory bodies, business ownership terminology, dish names, commodity examples and service conventions, provided the function described is correct. Where a candidate cites a non-UK body, credit it if its stated role (standard setting, CPD, industry representation) is accurate.

**Temperatures and quantities.** Accept the correct figure with the correct direction of travel. A bare figure with no indication of "below/at or above/between" is ambiguous and should not be credited where the demand is for a *safe operating* temperature. Accept a correct range or a correct single value within the accepted range; accept °C without the symbol; do not credit Fahrenheit conversions that are inaccurate. Where the scheme gives a threshold plus a preferred figure, either alone earns the mark.

**Technical terminology and spelling.** Credit phonetically recognisable spellings of micro-organisms, commodities and techniques where the intended term is unambiguous. Do not credit a spelling that produces a different, incorrect term.

**Repetition and overlap.** Two responses that are the same point in different words score once. In tabular questions, the same example may not be used to earn marks in two different rows.

**Unsafe or discriminatory content.** A fluent, well-structured answer that recommends unsafe food handling, non-compliant temperature control, or a discriminatory approach to customers with particular requirements cannot be credited for those points and cannot access Band 4, however well written.

**Blank and irrelevant responses.** Award 0. Do not award "effort" marks. A response that answers a different question from the one set scores 0 even if accurate.

**Rubric infringement.** All questions in both papers are compulsory; there is no choice, so no rubric-error rules apply. Mark everything the candidate offers.

**Portfolio moderation.** Centre marks must be supported by evidence: photographic or video record of the practical, the costed plan, the finished dish assessment, and the two written investigations with presentation evidence. Where evidence for AO3 is absent or is purely written description, the AO3 mark cannot stand.

---

## 6. Common Candidate Errors

- **Internal/external customer confusion.** Candidates frequently offer a colleague from another department as an "external" customer or a supplier/contractor as "internal." Costs the mark outright — the distinction is the discriminator in these items.
- **Naming instead of defining.** In tabular cooking-method questions, giving only the method name where the demand is "define one way in which… can be cooked" loses the row mark. Insist on the mechanism, medium or temperature.
- **Pathogens confused with illnesses or non-bacteria.** Listing a foodborne *illness*, a virus, a mould or "food poisoning" itself where **pathogenic bacteria** are demanded gains nothing. Only bacterial genera/species are creditable.
- **Commodity/method category slippage.** Offering a commodity where a method is asked (or vice versa), or placing an item in the wrong commodity row of a table (e.g. a crustacean listed under "fish"). Mark the row wrong; do not transfer credit between rows.
- **Answering one half of a two-part scenario.** The single most common cap on Paper 2-A. A response covering only (i) is limited to Band 2 at best, however strong.
- **Generic, un-applied theory.** Reciting textbook material on teamwork or customer service without touching the specific problem in the vignette holds a response in Band 2.
- **Assertion without evaluation.** "Teamwork is good for business" with no stated benefit (retention, sales, image, repeat custom) forfeits the AO4 element and blocks Bands 3–4.
- **Repeating one point to fill the tariff.** In "state/describe two…" items this yields one mark only.
- **Temperature given without direction.** A number alone in the hot-holding and chilled-storage items.
- **Ignoring the response form.** Continuous prose where slide content is required, or a single undifferentiated block where a two-part guidance summary is required, weakens the top-band criterion on presentation, though correct content is still credited.
- **Vague customer-requirement answers.** "Help them" or "be nice" for customers with mobility or hearing needs. Credit requires a specific, practicable provision.

---

**Standardisation note:** examiners must mark the standardisation sample before live marking and must refer any answer that is credible, safe and correct but falls outside the indicative content to the Principal Examiner before awarding — such answers are usually creditable and, once agreed, are added to the live addendum for the series.
